a-only-http: All traffic goes to A; B and C are idle. This is the baseline.
a-only-grpc: All calls go to A; B and C are idle. Baseline.
round-robin-http: Requests are handed out in turn, so each replica gets 1/3. p95 is unchanged from A-only: 40 req/s is far below what one replica can handle, so spreading the load does not make it faster.
round-robin-grpc: Calls are routed one by one (HTTP/2 listener), so 1/3 each even though the client uses one connection. p95 unchanged for the same reason as HTTP.
weighted-http: Shares follow the weights (A takes 2 of every 4 requests). A higher weight sends more work to A but adds no capacity; p95 shows no gain beyond run-to-run noise because no replica was near its limit.
weighted-grpc: Same as HTTP: exactly 50/25/25. No latency gain, no extra capacity.
delay-rr-http: Round robin ignores speed: slow B still gets 1/3, so a third of requests wait 400 ms and p95 sits at about the delay.
delay-rr-grpc: Same as HTTP: B keeps 1/3 of the calls and p95 is about the 400 ms delay.
delay-lr-http: Least request moves traffic away from busy B: B drops to 12.7 %, A and C take about 44 % each. p95 stays near 410 ms because B still gets more than 5 % of requests; the share of slow requests fell from 33 % to 13 %.
delay-lr-grpc: Same as HTTP: B 13.2 %. p95 stays near 410 ms for the same reason.
failure-http: Envoy kept sending B its share (about 13 req/s) until two health checks failed (5.2 s after B stopped): 69 requests got 503 (1.9 %), no retries. A and C then took 50 % each. B was healthy again 4.8 s after it started. B's total share is 22 % because it served only part of the 90 s.
failure-grpc: Same pattern: removal 4.7 s, 65 calls failed with UNAVAILABLE (1.8 %), recovery 4.3 s after B started.
